- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.75) and forecast is above recent high, reduce forecast slightly to avoid overreaction.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5) and forecast is below recent low, increase forecast gently to avoid underreaction.  
- If forecast peaks sharply after a spike in sentiment, cap the overshoot by reducing 5–10% of the peak value.  
- For 30-day horizons, if true outcome deviates >10% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast toward that average.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., +0.5 → -0.5 → +0.5), apply mean reversion bias toward prior 7-day average.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.33) and forecast is consistently above true outcome, reduce forecast by 2–5% to align with low volatility.  
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if true outcome is below 30% of 30d forecast, apply downward correction proportional to sentiment decay.
